raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're starting in the West Village, right at Washington Square Park, so take a moment and take it in.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Half the stories on this block were secrets when they happened — and the first one is hiding on a façade above your head.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Look up at 82 Washington Place.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"From about 1908 to 1913, this was home to the novelist Willa Cather and her partner, Edith Lewis.","source_id":"a4b5feda-f6d1-4f1e-b326-24622abea44e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Cather wrote My Ántonia and Death Comes for the Archbishop, had two central relationships with women, and as an undergraduate at the University of Nebraska signed her letters to a woman she admired as 'William.'","source_id":"a4b5feda-f6d1-4f1e-b326-24622abea44e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The two of them stayed together at addresses around the Village for nearly forty years, until Cather died in 1947.","source_id":"a4b5feda-f6d1-4f1e-b326-24622abea44e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"But she guarded that life fiercely — she burned most of her personal letters before she died, and the one surviving college note laments her 'unnatural' attraction to another woman.","source_id":"a4b5feda-f6d1-4f1e-b326-24622abea44e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"A few steps on, at 86 University Place, a very different door once opened.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In the 1950s this was the Bagatelle, one of the only lesbian bars in the whole city, alongside the more working-class Sea Colony and the Swing Rendezvous.","source_id":"566345ed-1334-48c0-bd37-1154fa49baac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The poet and essayist Audre Lorde wrote about it in her autobiography, Zami: A New Spelling of My Name.","source_id":"566345ed-1334-48c0-bd37-1154fa49baac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"There was a tiny dance floor in back, and the front room, she remembered, 'smelled like plastic and blue glass and beer and lots of good-looking young women.'","source_id":"566345ed-1334-48c0-bd37-1154fa49baac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Out and Black, Lorde and the other women like her rarely acknowledged one another inside — and yet, as she put it, 'the Bag was always The Club.'","source_id":"566345ed-1334-48c0-bd37-1154fa49baac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Now picture 125 East Eleventh Street roaring.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"From 1913 through the 1930s, Webster Hall there threw the annual Greenwich Village Ball — masquerade nights for the neighborhood's bohemians, many of them gay men in drag.","source_id":"88c68795-b8f3-4892-80d3-7b8260efcc6f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"By the early 1920s, gay men and lesbians were holding events of their own there.","source_id":"88c68795-b8f3-4892-80d3-7b8260efcc6f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In 1934 the New York Herald Tribune tried to capture the scene: 'Men danced with women in men's clothes. Women danced with men in women's clothes. And strange androgynous couples careened about the floor, oblivious to the workings of society and nature.'","source_id":"88c68795-b8f3-4892-80d3-7b8260efcc6f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Today it's a popular, mostly straight nightclub.","source_id":"88c68795-b8f3-4892-80d3-7b8260efcc6f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"From the 1920s into the 1950s, 171 West Twelfth Street held a whole network of lesbian couples and comrades: the artist Nancy Cook and the educator Marion Dickerman; the activist Polly Porter and the Democratic official Molly Dewson; and Grace Hutchins and Anna Rochester, both Communist Party leaders.","source_id":"ddffc7ef-5d80-45be-bb5b-f15fa6a70eaa","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Cook and Dickerman especially were close friends with Eleanor Roosevelt, who kept apartments nearby at 20 East Eleventh Street and later at 29 Washington Square West.","source_id":"ddffc7ef-5d80-45be-bb5b-f15fa6a70eaa","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"When Franklin became president, Eleanor turned into a fierce champion for women in government, and her friends landed New Deal posts — Dewson ran the Women's Division of the Democratic National Committee, while the president's appointees included Frances Perkins, the first woman in a cabinet, and Grace Abbott of the Children's Bureau.","source_id":"ddffc7ef-5d80-45be-bb5b-f15fa6a70eaa","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Eleanor had her own intimate relationship, with the Associated Press reporter Lorena Hickok, assigned in 1932 to cover the new first lady; their letters read as passionate, though many biographers still strenuously insist Roosevelt was not a lesbian.","source_id":"ddffc7ef-5d80-45be-bb5b-f15fa6a70eaa","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"One last house — 457 Sixth Avenue.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"This was home to Murray Hall, a Tammany Hall 'ward heeler' who organized the vote right here in this district.","source_id":"653d8107-500f-4e60-9e2a-c9a79ea18077","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Married twice, a heavy drinker, a brawler, and by all accounts 'sweet on women,' Hall died in 1901, leaving a wife and an adopted daughter.","source_id":"653d8107-500f-4e60-9e2a-c9a79ea18077","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"And then the revelation: Hall had died of breast cancer, and had been a woman who passed as a man for all of her adult life.","source_id":"653d8107-500f-4e60-9e2a-c9a79ea18077","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The New York Times ran the story for days.","source_id":"653d8107-500f-4e60-9e2a-c9a79ea18077","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"One lawyer friend simply couldn't accept it: 'I saw him play poker like a veteran... I just can't believe he was a woman, that's all' — still calling Hall 'he.'","source_id":"653d8107-500f-4e60-9e2a-c9a79ea18077","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0}]}
